why: A (universes 0), for slice submanifolds N ⊆ V with the induced metric only: (i) c ∈ Ω(N;p,q) is a critical path of E (all variations IsVariation, any open U ⊆ ℝ, any break set) iff the first-variation functional -Σ⟨W,Δ_tV⟩-∫⟨W,A⟩ vanishes on TΩ_c (Theorem 12.2 + Lemma 11.A); (ii) at an unbroken geodesic (IsUnbrokenGeodesic: C^∞ on [0,1], geodesic on (0,1)) the first variation vanishes in every direction. B, for every abstract connected Hausdorff ℝⁿ-manifold with any smooth metric and any Levi-Civita connection: (1) IsGeodesic on [0,1] ⇔ C^∞ on [0,1] with D/dt dω/dt existing and identically 0 — a restatement of B's own definition, proved outright (geodesic_iff_def, no hypothesis); (2) geodesic ⇒ critical path of E. A ⇒ B fails genuinely: abstract manifolds (no first variation formula / variations on abstract M in the project). B ⇒ A fails genuinely: A's characterization of criticality by the first-variation functional (isCriticalPath_iff) is not a consequence of B, which only says geodesics are critical.
overlap: No A_to_B/B_to_A. Embedded theorems: B_to_A_geod_crit shares 107 project theorems, A_to_B_emb 101 — all infrastructure: slice-chart/atlas/gram lemmas, the structure fields of IsVariation and IsGeodesicOn, tanProj/tanCoord lemmas, piecewise_induction, continuousOn_of_piecewise, projRep (via Bridge); none of the argument (first_variation, exists_variation_one, hasDerivAt_energy are not shared).
